name: Move equipment between pads and bases
summary: A frac fleet is 30 to 50 heavy units: pump trailers, blender, data van, chemical units, iron and manifold trailers, sand storage, light towers and crew trucks. Moving it from one pad, or from a district base after maintenance, to the next pad takes route planning, oversize and overweight permits, checks of road bans and county road use rules, and booking company tractors, Class 1 operators and third-party carriers for the units the fleet cannot pull itself. The operations coordinator, a service dispatcher, the field supervisor, the pump operators who drive the tractors, and sometimes the district manager, a field mechanic and outside carriers take part. Spring thaw road bans, winter storms, soft lease roads and drivers' hours limits decide when a move can start, and a move often needs two trips because there are fewer drivers than trailers.

baseline.org_archetype: A Canadian pressure pumping company with six to eight crewed frac fleets working multi-well pads in Alberta and northeast BC from district bases, with a Calgary engineering and sales office.
baseline.notes: Common practice of large WCSB pressure pumpers in 2019-2022: ERP, spreadsheets, email and phone, fracture modelling software and a data van acquisition system; no automated scheduling optimiser.

unit_of_work: one fleet move (pad to pad, or base to pad)
trigger: The pad program's mobilization plan or the rig-down at the previous pad gives the units to move, origin, destination and target arrival.
end_state: All units staged on the new lease and handed to the rig-up crew, carrier tickets reconciled and the fleet location updated.

volume.seasonality: Few moves in April and May under road bans; a burst of moves when bans lift; most moves December to March and June to November.

evidence.note: One move into each pad (about 18 a month) plus occasional base trips for maintenance; slightly below the organisation file's 8-20-30 because pad-corridor work avoids some moves.

surge.cause: Post-break-up restart when road bans lift and fleets move out together

evidence.note: Spring and post-thaw weight periods are set by thaw depth and dates (src3); the multiplier is an estimate.
Move list and load count for each move; estimate.
Route checks, permits, truck booking and close-out; estimate. Not listed among the organisation file's roles for this process.
Approves spot-rate carriers on a minority of moves; estimate.
Journey plan, departure decision and arrival check-in; estimate.
About 22 Class 1 operators drive tractors on each move, often with a second trip; estimate.
Roadside repairs on breakdowns; estimate. Not listed among the organisation file's roles for this process.

steps.name: Receive move requirement
steps.description: The operations coordinator receives the mobilization plan with the fleet, origin, destination legal land location and target arrival from the pad program, or a rig-down notice from the field supervisor at the current pad.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Build the move list and load count
steps.description: The coordinator lists every unit by number with dimensions and gross and axle weights from the fleet roster, marks which units company tractors pull and which need carriers, cranes or pilot vehicles, and counts trips needed for the drivers available.

error.defect_description: A unit missed or its weight understated

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Check road bans and plan the route
steps.description: The dispatcher checks the provincial road ban list and county and municipal ban orders, bridge limits and county road use rules along candidate routes, calls the producer about lease road condition, and picks a route that keeps loaded units legal.

error.defect_description: A municipal ban or bridge limit missed on a local road

next.condition: bans or road conditions block the move

evidence.note: Provincial and municipal road bans reduce allowed weights during thaw (src3); times estimated.

steps.name: Wait for bans to lift or roads to firm
steps.description: Loaded pump trailers cannot travel while seasonal bans or soft lease roads hold; the fleet waits at the old pad or base until a ban percentage changes, a frost window opens or the producer firms the road.

evidence.note: Thaw-based ban periods (src3); wait durations estimated.

steps.name: Arrange county road use approval
steps.description: The dispatcher contacts the county or municipal district for a road use agreement or ban exemption for the local roads to the lease, fills the request form and waits for written approval.

evidence.note: Local road bans set by counties and municipal districts, with exemption permits (src3); times estimated.

steps.name: Apply for oversize and overweight permits
steps.description: For units not covered by annual permits the dispatcher enters each move in the provincial TRAVIS permitting system: unit, axle weights, dimensions, route and dates, and pays the fee.

control.basis: Alberta Commercial Vehicle Dimension and Weight Regulation; oversize and overweight permits through TRAVIS

evidence.note: Permit applications through TRAVIS Web or an agent (src4); time estimated.

steps.name: Wait for permit approval
steps.description: The provincial permit office reviews the application; routine routes are issued automatically or within hours, unusual loads or routes take days or come back with a changed route.

evidence.note: TRAVIS reviews of up to four business days for single trip permits (src5); most fleet units moved under routine permits (estimate).

steps.name: Book tractors, drivers and carriers
steps.description: The dispatcher assigns company tractors and Class 1 operators, checks each driver's hours and off-duty days, and books outside carriers for sand storage, crane, light towers, tanks and pilot cars.

error.defect_description: A driver booked who is out of hours

control.basis: Commercial Vehicle Drivers Hours of Service Regulations, oil well service vehicle permit conditions

evidence.note: Oil well service vehicle permit off-duty rules (src12); time estimated.

steps.name: Wait for carrier confirmation
steps.description: Outside carriers confirm trucks and drivers for the move day, or report they cannot cover it in a busy period.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Approve spot-rate carrier
steps.description: The district manager approves using a spot carrier at a higher rate, or moving the move date, after comparing the cost with fleet standby at the new pad.

control.basis: Delegated spending authority for third-party trucking

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Prepare the journey management plan
steps.description: The field supervisor writes the journey plan: convoy order, route hazards, check-in points and times, radio channel, pilot vehicle positions and what to do on a breakdown, and files it with HSE.

control.basis: Company journey management procedure under the OHS hazard assessment duty

evidence.note: Hazard assessment duty (src11); journey management practice is an estimate.

steps.name: Pre-trip inspections on move day
steps.description: When the last stage at the old pad is pumped and units are rigged down, operators do circle checks on tractors and trailers: brakes, lights, tires, chains and load securement, and start their electronic logs.

control.basis: National Safety Code trip inspection requirements for commercial vehicles

evidence.note: Trip inspections are a commercial vehicle requirement (not opened here); the wait is the time until the previous pad finishes and rig-down ends.

steps.name: Decide to depart
steps.description: The field supervisor checks the weather, road reports and daylight, and holds the convoy if visibility, ice or wind make oversize travel unsafe or not permitted.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Drive the convoy to the new pad
steps.description: Operators drive the tractors and units in convoy over highways, county roads and the lease road, checking in at the planned points; travel is often one to four hours each way.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Carriers haul storage, crane and support units
steps.description: Outside carriers haul the sand storage units, crane, light towers and tanks on the same day, arriving in the order the spotting plan needs.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Recover a broken-down or stuck unit
steps.description: A field mechanic drives out to fix a tire, air or electrical fault, or arranges a winch or tow for a unit stuck on a soft lease road.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Return for the second load
steps.description: Because there are fewer drivers and tractors than trailers, a group of operators drives back to the old pad or base for the remaining units and repeats the haul.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Check in at the lease
steps.description: The field supervisor reports arrival to the producer's wellsite supervisor and checks that the lease is open; if the lease is not ready, units stage at the lease entrance or a staging area.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Wait for lease access
steps.description: Units wait at the staging area until the producer's drilling rig or other contractors clear the pad or the lease road is repaired.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Hand units to the rig-up crew
steps.description: The field supervisor confirms every unit on the move list has arrived and is staged, and releases the move to the rig-up crew and the coordinator.

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

steps.name: Close out the move
steps.description: The dispatcher updates unit locations on the dispatch board and ERP, checks driver hours in telematics, matches carrier tickets to bookings and passes them to accounts payable.

error.defect_description: Carrier ticket hours not checked against bookings

evidence.note: Author's estimate from general knowledge of WCSB pressure pumping operations.

exceptions.name: Road ban or soft road hold
exceptions.description: Seasonal bans or soft lease roads stop loaded units; the move waits days.

exceptions.name: County road use approval
exceptions.description: Local road use agreement or ban exemption needed from a county.

exceptions.name: No regular carrier
exceptions.description: District manager approves a spot carrier or a later date.

exceptions.name: Breakdown en route
exceptions.description: A unit breaks down or gets stuck and a field mechanic recovers it.

exceptions.name: Lease not accessible
exceptions.description: Units stage until the producer opens the pad.

benchmarks.unit: days from move requirement received to move closed out (units handed to rig-up plus ticket close-out)

evidence.note: Estimate: moves are planned about a week ahead and executed in one to two days; long tails from road bans and lease access.

benchmarks.metric: TRAVIS single trip over-dimensional review time (City of Calgary)
benchmarks.population: City of Calgary single trip permits

evidence.note: City of Calgary page (src5); provincial routine permits are often faster.

pain_points.description: Spring thaw road bans and municipal bans can stop a move for days, idling a fleet and crew.

evidence.note: Road ban periods set by thaw depth (src3).

pain_points.description: Fewer drivers than trailers means second trips, stretching the move and drivers' hours.

evidence.note: Driver off-duty rules (src12); second-trip share estimated.

pain_points.description: Carrier availability is tight in peak months, forcing spot rates or date changes.

evidence.note: Estimate.

sources.title: Road bans
sources.supports: Road bans reduce maximum weights on roads during weak or thawing conditions; provincial road ban list and municipal bans for local roads; notification service for ban orders; Road Ban Exemption Permit Request to the Central Permit Office; spring heavy-haul period starts when thaw depth reaches 25 cm, post-thaw from about June 16, summer July 1.

sources.title: Commercial vehicle oversize and overweight permits
sources.supports: Oversize and overweight permits applied for through TRAVIS Web or a TRAVIS agent; some permits only through the Central Permit Office; fees set by the Commercial Vehicle Dimension and Weight Regulation; travel on banned roads prohibited above ban percentages.

sources.title: Over-dimensional permit
sources.supports: TRAVIS is the Government of Alberta permitting system; single trip over-dimensional applications through TRAVIS may take up to 4 business days for review; annual permits five business days.

sources.title: Occupational Health and Safety Code (legislation search)
sources.supports: OHS Code Part 2 Hazard Assessment, Elimination and Control, section 7 Hazard assessment and section 8 Worker participation.

sources.title: Commercial Vehicle Drivers Hours of Service Regulations (SOR/2005-313), section 63, version in force 2019-06-12 to 2021-06-11
sources.publisher: Justice Laws Website, Government of Canada
sources.supports: Oil well service vehicle permits: at least three 24-hour off-duty periods in any 24 days, 72 consecutive hours off after permit driving, waiting time at a well site may be logged off duty if no work is done; permit requires field safety training.

assumptions: Loaded hourly costs are taken from the organisation file.
Volume 8-18-28 moves a month, a little below the organisation file's 8-20-30, since pad-corridor work lets a fleet move short distances without a full mobilization.
Tractor occupied minutes are summed over about 22 tractors on the main haul and 10 on a second trip.
The move permit is produced by the transport regulator in response to the dispatcher's application; the interface keeps the organisation file's direction.
The service dispatcher does most of the permit and booking work but is not listed in the organisation file's process_map roles; the field mechanic and outside trucking carrier also take part.
The pre-trip inspection wait is the time between the move being planned and the previous pad finishing; it dominates elapsed time.

Simulated median of about 8.4 days is above the 7-day estimate because the permit and carrier waits are modelled in sequence; in practice the dispatcher often books carriers while permits are pending, so the real median is likely nearer 6-7 days.

Resource cost in the simulation applies the fleet's running cost per hour to hours it is held idle waiting for bans or lease access, so it overstates cash cost; the hours themselves are the useful measure of lost fleet time.
